I would avoid putting anything from University of Phoenix on a resume.

I went to an average state college and by my senior year I was really considering going to grad-school to get a masters degree. One of the reasons I wanted to do this was because I had a friend who was teaching at UoP and really liked it, He only worked ~5 hours a week and made (on the side) about $15,000 a year. But you needed a masters to teach there (at least then in 2009, not sure if you still need one).

So during a casual conversation with my department head I mentioned that after I get my masters I was going to try to teach at an online university, specifically UoP.

He said don't do it.

I went on how getting some extra money would help, yada, yada, yada.

He went on to say that at this college, and all the other ones in the state, having anything from UoP (and a handful of other online colleges) would completely bar you form working at the college. He said that he got at least 10 resumes a week to his department and if there was anything form taking a course at or teaching at UoP the resume went in the trash.

You wouldn't even get accepted to the graduate programs if you had any UoP classes on your transcripts. They would make you retake those courses as an undergrad before acceptance.

Even undergrads were "advised" to retake UoP courses before they were allowed to graduate.

And he said that this was not "uncommon" for universities to do, even though it wasn't "stated".

TLDR: Don't "go" to University of Phoenix, but if you did, don't put it on your resume, and if you ever taught there, don't put it on your resume if you want to teach or work at another university.

This is really interesting! Thanks for sharing. It seems like for-profit schools like UoP are consistently getting bad press/getting shut down. All I've ever heard is that they're usually not a great deal for students, a little skeevy all around.

I don't want to waste too much time solving this, and would rather go back to vs2013 for the moment if it'll take a long time. Possible solutions I can think of, but want to confirm a little first:

Thanks!

SOLVED: I had linked entityx's debug version to my release version incorrectly. Silly mistake now fixed, with my FPS now more than double (157 FPS) what it was before. Thanks to /u/rwbj for helping me out.

If everything's running just dandy there then you can at least isolate the problem to the new base project. And on that topic of course also check for similar optimization/release settings for the new project itself. I'm not sure if these are carried over consistently in the import process.
